subject.title: feat: contextual group activation — LLM-driven peeking/engaged state machine

question: Should OpenClaw support model-driven contextual activation for unmentioned group traffic, and if so should it live in core shared activation, a plugin/channel API seam, or a narrower attention-window mode?
rationale: Automation can prove the missing mode, but it cannot choose the privacy boundary, provider exposure, retained decision logs, config contract, channel coverage, or long-term owner for processing unmentioned group traffic.

options.title: Sponsor default-off design first
options.body: Approve a maintainer-owned design with explicit consent, provider exposure, retention/logging, config schema, channel coverage, and tests before accepting code.

options.title: Narrow to attention behavior
options.body: Pursue timer-based attention windows or ambient room-event ergonomics without adding a model-driven background peeking path yet.

options.title: Defer to plugin/API seam
options.body: Wait for or design the observation and decision-hook API needed to keep this optional policy outside core runtime defaults.

recommendation.title: Sponsor default-off design first
recommendation.body: Approve a maintainer-owned design with explicit consent, provider exposure, retention/logging, config schema, channel coverage, and tests before accepting code.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses the activation command, shared mention policy, and channel ingress boundaries that steipete introduced or recently centralized.
